title: Plural negative questions: Eivätkö nämä ole…?
summary: Build plural negative yes/no questions with eivätkö and ole.
objectives: Begin a plural negative question with eivätkö.
Keep the supplied plural subject before ole.
Contrast plural eivätkö with singular eikö.

sections.title: See the pattern
paragraphs: A plural negative yes/no question begins with Eivätkö.
Eivätkö contains the plural negative verb eivät and the front-vowel question suffix -kö.

sections.title: Use one clear decision
paragraphs: The plural demonstrative subject follows, and ole remains the main verb.
Read number and polarity before choosing the opening word.

steps: nämä kirjat: the complete subject is supplied.
nuo kirjat: the complete subject is supplied.

examples.english: Aren't the previously identified books at home?
steps: ne kirjat: the complete subject is supplied.

commonMistakes: Do not use eikö with a plural subject.
Do not omit ole after the subject.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Choose the sentence that means “Aren't the previously identified cars here?” During a guided tour. Use the supplied phrase ne autot (“the previously identified cars”) and täällä (“here”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Eivätkö carries plural negative agreement and -ko/-kö; ole follows later in the question.

optionFeedback.Eivätkö ne autot ole täällä?: Correct. Eivätkö carries plural negative agreement and -ko/-kö; ole follows later in the question.
optionFeedback.Eikö ne autot ole täällä?: “Eikö” is the singular negative question verb; use “Eivätkö”, the plural negative question verb.
“Eivät” is the plural negative verb; use “Eivätkö”, the plural negative question verb.
optionFeedback.Ovatko ne autot täällä?: “Ovatko” is the plural affirmative question verb; use “Eivätkö”, the plural negative question verb.
